privacyFacts: An account is required. Sign-in and sign-up go through Clerk; the backend keeps a user record keyed by the Clerk id and email (src/api.ts getUser/createUser, src/app/_layout.tsx).

Logged data (food, workouts, body records, plans, supplements, soreness, gyms) is stored on the OmegaFyt backend: an ASP.NET Core API on Fly.io (region iad, US) with a PostgreSQL database (FitnessBackend/Readme.MD, fly.toml, .junie/guidelines.md).

With health sync on, weigh-ins imported from Apple Health or Health Connect are saved to the OmegaFyt backend (src/lib/health.ios.ts and health.android.ts importWeights, FitnessBackend HealthKitService.cs).
Food search, autocomplete and barcode lookups go through the backend to the FatSecret Platform API (FitnessBackend/FoodApi/FatSecretApi.cs).
The iOS and Android apps send product analytics events, screen names, tap events and error reports to PostHog when the build has a PostHog key; the web build sends none (src/lib/analytics.ts).

Analytics events exclude weight, height, sex and measurements, but include plan choices such as goal, weekly pace, plan length and training days. Tap autocapture records component names, testID and ph-label, never the tapped text. No session replay is configured (README.md, src/lib/analytics-provider.tsx, OnboardingFlow.tsx stepProperties).

Purchases go through RevenueCat with App Store and Google Play billing. On iOS, RevenueCat collects Apple Search Ads attribution through the AdServices token, which needs no App Tracking Transparency prompt (src/lib/purchases.ts).

Health sync is off until the user turns it on, and it can be turned off in Settings. It reads weight and steps and writes weight and daily calories, protein, carbs and fat (src/lib/health.ios.ts, src/lib/health.android.ts, src/lib/health.shared.ts).

Delete account is in Settings and on the forced paywall: backend data is deleted first, then the Clerk login. The backend also deletes account data when a Clerk user.deleted webhook arrives, if the webhook secret is configured (src/components/settings/DeleteAccount.tsx, src/app/paywall.tsx, FitnessBackend/.junie/guidelines.md).

Small preferences and the onboarding plan summary (onboarding status, rest timer, health sync settings) are stored on the device in SecureStore on native and localStorage on web (src/lib/utils.ts, src/lib/onboarding.ts).
The camera permission is requested for barcode scanning; microphone access is disabled and RECORD_AUDIO is blocked on Android (app.json).
omegafyt.businessModel: Subscription. The product is "OmegaFyt Pro" (RevenueCat entitlement id "pro"), sold through the App Store and Google Play via RevenueCat. On iOS and Android, a signed-in account without the entitlement is sent to a paywall it cannot dismiss; a new account sees guided setup first unless it falls in the onboarding experiment's control group. From the forced paywall the only ways forward are subscribing, restoring a purchase, signing out or deleting the account. The paywall lists whatever packages the current RevenueCat offering holds, and a PostHog flag can pick a different offering. No prices are in code. The web build has no checkout.

subscription.account: Required. Clerk handles sign-in and sign-up: the native Clerk AuthView on iOS, the AuthView with a hosted-browser fallback on Android, and the Clerk web SignIn on web. The enabled sign-in methods live in the Clerk dashboard, not in code; the README tells the developer to enable email, phone and username plus Apple, Google and GitHub SSO, and app.json carries the Google client IDs and the expo-apple-authentication plugin. The Clerk user id is also the RevenueCat app user id and the PostHog distinct id.
subscription.backend: ASP.NET Core Web API on .NET 10 (FitnessBackend), deployed to Fly.io (app fitnessapi-black-breeze-3375, region iad) with PostgreSQL via EF Core. It provides accounts, food logging backed by the FatSecret Platform API (search, autocomplete, barcode, food details), macro target generation, the workout store, a program generator with saved gyms, progressive overload recommendations, one-rep max estimates for 11 tracked lifts, trend weight, expenditure and body fat estimates, supplements, soreness, step goals, health weight import (used by both Apple Health and Health Connect sync), S3-compatible storage for progress photos (a feature the app does not link to today), and RevenueCat and Clerk webhooks.
packageTypes: Packages come from the RevenueCat offering, not from code
Code labels weekly, monthly, 2-month, 3-month, 6-month and annual packages as recurring prices
Code labels a lifetime package as a one-time price; the backend stores lifetime purchases as non-expiring
subscription.sync: All data lives on the backend, so the same account and data open on iPhone, Android and the web build. Subscriptions and health sync exist only in the native apps; the web build has no checkout and no paywall gate in the client.
thirdParties: RevenueCat (subscriptions, entitlement webhook, Apple Search Ads attribution on iOS)
Apple App Store and Google Play (billing)
PostHog (product analytics, feature flags, error tracking; native only)
FatSecret Platform API (food database, via the backend)
S3-compatible object storage (progress photo files; the feature is not reachable in the app today)
Apple HealthKit and Android Health Connect (opt-in; imported weights are saved to the backend)
subscription.trial: Not fixed in code. The paywall shows a free trial or intro price only if the store product has one and RevenueCat reports the user as eligible (Android: any intro price Google Play returns). Trial length and price are set in App Store Connect, Google Play and RevenueCat.
subscription.whatIsFree: Creating an account and, on iOS and Android, the guided setup. Setup saves units, sex, height, weight and a plan, shows calorie and macro targets, and builds or starts a first training program before the paywall; the backend exempts those endpoints from the subscription check. There is no ongoing free tier on iOS or Android.
subscription.whatRequiresSubscription: On iOS and Android, everything after setup: the Home, Workout, Eat, Supplements and Reports tabs and their screens sit behind the forced paywall for accounts without the pro entitlement. The backend can also gate every data endpoint server side (Entitlements:Enforce), but that switch is off by default.

caveats: Macro targets, projected end weight, energy expenditure, body fat (US Navy formula) and one-rep max (Epley formula) are estimates, not medical advice. Calorie targets start from a rule of thumb of 15 Cal per pound of trend weight, adjusted for the plan, and are shown as a narrow range.

Release status: onboarding, the personalized paywall, PostHog analytics, the program builder, saved gyms and the rest timer all landed between 2026-09-29 and 2026-10-02 (app bumped to 1.8.0 on 2026-10-02, backend c89ff3c on 2026-10-02). Earlier public builds were 1.7.0. Confirm the 1.8.0 store release and the backend deploy and migration before the site markets these features. On a backend without the generator, the builder shows "Not available yet" and onboarding falls back to a Workout Store program.
No prices, trial length or plan lineup are in code. They live in App Store Connect, Google Play and RevenueCat. Do not state prices or promise a free trial.

Subscriptions can be bought only in the iOS and Android apps. The web build has no checkout and no client-side paywall, so do not market the web build as free or as included with a plan; describe it only as the same account in a browser.
No public web URL is in either repo; confirm the Vercel deployment before linking to a web app.
The food database is the FatSecret Platform API, reached through the backend. Its size is not in code, so do not quote a food count. The app shows no FatSecret attribution today.
142 is the number of exercises in the program generator catalog migration. The full exercise library lives in the production database and its total is not in code, so do not quote an exercise count.

One-rep max estimates cover only 11 tracked lifts (Incline Bench Press, Bench Press, Chest Dip, Squat, Leg Press, Deadlift, Sumo Deadlift, Shoulder Press, Pull-Up, Chin-Up, Barbell Row) and only sets logged with weight above zero.
Body fat needs a height and neck and navel measurements (plus hip for the female formula); the male formula is used only when sex is set to male.
Onboarding is a PostHog experiment: the control variant skips it and goes straight to the paywall. Onboarding never runs on web.
Health sync, the steps card, rest notifications, setup and purchases are native only.
Steps are read from Apple Health or Health Connect. The app does not count steps itself.
No iPad version (supportsTablet is false). English only, with numbers and dates in the device's regional format.
An account and a network connection to the backend are required. There is no offline mode.
Expenditure needs at least 2 weigh-ins and 3 logged days of more than 500 Cal in a 14-day window. With less data it falls back to a weight multiple or 2,000.

Blood pressure logging: client API functions exist (src/api.ts), but there are no screens.
Server-side subscription enforcement (Entitlements:Enforce) is off by default.
Web purchases and subscription management on web.
Over-the-air updates: app.json and the native configs carry an EAS Update URL, but the expo-updates package is not installed, so do not claim instant updates.
In-app feedback: the backend has PostFeedback endpoints, but the app has no feedback screen.
Widgets, Live Activities, Apple Watch and Wear OS apps: the design-system doc covers these for the other Vector apps; OmegaFyt has a single app target and no extensions.
iPad support (supportsTablet is false).
Languages other than English (supportedLocales is en only).
Writing waist circumference to Apple Health: the permission is requested but the app never writes it.

privacyFacts: No account or sign-in. There is no auth code in src/, and docs/app-store/review-notes.md states no account is required.

No network calls in app code. A search of src/ finds no fetch, XMLHttpRequest, WebSocket or HTTP client. The only URLs are four citation links on the Sources & methods screen, opened in the system browser via Linking.openURL (src/lib/metric-sources.ts, src/app/health-sources.tsx:14).

All records live in an on-device SQLite database (expo-sqlite with Drizzle, src/db/index.ts, src/db/schema.ts): weight entries, measurements, preferences, photo file names and health-link mappings.

privacyFacts: No account and no sign-in. The Settings screen states: Vector Lift keeps everything on this phone. No account, no servers. (src/lib/locales/en.json localOnlyNote, src/components/screens/settings-screen.tsx)

No network code: a search of src, modules and targets finds no fetch, XMLHttpRequest, axios, WebSocket or URLSession calls, and package.json has no networking, analytics, crash-reporting or over-the-air update SDK.
No analytics or tracking. src/lib/analytics.ts only computes Progress summaries from local workouts on demand and stores nothing.
All records live in a local SQLite database (lift_track.db) through Drizzle. The exercise library ships in the app bundle and updates only with app updates.
Nothing in the code excludes the database from the operating system's own device backups, so an iCloud or Android device backup the user has turned on may include it.

Health sync is off by default and goes through the OS (HealthKit or Health Connect). When on, it reads and writes body weight and writes finished workouts with their name and start and end times, using only the permissions granted.

The Apple Watch app asks HealthKit for permission to run a strength-training session and read heart rate. It shows live heart rate and discards that session at the end; the phone writes the one Health workout.

Backups are files the user saves through the share sheet: AES-256-GCM with a key from PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 at 600,000 iterations and a random 16-byte salt. Passwords are at least 10 characters, are not stored and cannot be recovered.
Restore writes an encrypted recovery copy of current records first and replaces everything in one database transaction.
Erase all data deletes every personal table and app-held copies, overwrites deleted rows (secure_delete) and compacts the database. It does not touch files already shared or Health records.
CSV exports and pre-migration database copies are unencrypted.

On-device AI features call only the phone's own model: Apple Foundation Models SystemLanguageModel, never Private Cloud Compute, and the ML Kit GenAI Prompt API on Android, whose Gemini Nano model is installed by the system, not the app. There is no cloud fallback, and the app's copy of a program photo is deleted once read.
No in-app purchase or payment code exists in the app.

caveats: Progression rules are product heuristics built on RIR-based autoregulation and volume ideas, not individual prescriptions. Starting volumes, caps and set steps are choices, not validated thresholds (docs/progression.md Limits).

Health export writes strength-training workouts with a name and start and end times; no energy is estimated, so it does not report calories.
Backup passwords cannot be recovered, and restore replaces records rather than merging them.
Exercises carry one short text technique cue each; there are no exercise videos or illustrations.
iPhone only on iOS; iPad is not supported. The Apple Watch app is a companion that logs the phone's open workout and needs the iPhone app.

privacyFacts: No account and no sign-in: the code has no auth provider or login flow.

The app's own code makes no network requests: a search of src, modules, plugins and targets finds no fetch, XMLHttpRequest, WebSocket, URLSession or OkHttp use. Source, license and method links open in the system browser only.
No analytics or crash-reporting SDK in package.json (no Sentry, Firebase, Amplitude, Mixpanel, PostHog or expo-updates).

On Android, text recognition, the system barcode scanner and Gemini Nano are Google components (ML Kit, Google Play services code scanner, AICore). Their own data handling follows Google's terms and is outside what a code audit of this repo can confirm.
Food search and barcode lookup run against two bundled SQLite catalogs (usda.db and off.db) on the phone. The README states food search does not call a remote API.
Personal records live in a private on-device SQLite database (macro_track.db). It is not encrypted on the phone, like pre-migration copies.
Photo logging uses only on-device models. Photos are downscaled, deleted from the app cache when the logger closes, and not stored with diary entries.
Nutrition label photos are deleted once they have been read.

Encrypted backups use AES-256-GCM with PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 at 600,000 iterations. The password is not stored, there is no password recovery and there is no backup server; the user picks the destination in the share sheet, and a cloud destination uses that provider.
Apple Health and Health Connect sync is off until the user turns it on.

Erasure clears all personal tables, recovery backups, pre-migration copies and export cache, overwrites deleted rows and compacts the database when storage allows. It cannot delete copies shared outside the app or records already in Apple Health or Health Connect.
Bundled food catalogs are kept in the cache folder, which iCloud and Android backups skip.
On Android, a one-time Gemini Nano download is handled by the system AICore service when the user chooses it; it is a model download, not an upload of personal records.
macros.businessModel: Not implemented in code. There is no purchase, paywall or entitlement code and no StoreKit, RevenueCat or billing dependency. The product plan (docs/macro-track-plan.md) says a paid download or one-time core unlock fits the ownership proposition, that subscription versus lifetime pricing is undecided, and that any entitlement must keep ordinary offline use working without repeated server validation. The site owner groups this app with the single-purchase, always-offline apps, but no price or payment model is set anywhere in the repo. Do not show a price.
caveats: Coaching is for adults 18 and over who are not pregnant or breastfeeding. Medical nutrition needs and eating disorder care need professional guidance (coachingScopeBody in src/lib/locales/en.json).

The coaching method is the app's own approximate method. It is not clinically validated and is not MacroFactor's algorithm. Do not market it as validated, clinical or medical (docs/mvp-validation.md, Before public release item 2).
Check-ins propose changes; nothing changes targets until the user accepts or adjusts. Check-ins hold until there are at least 12 covered days and six weigh-in days in the last 21.
Expenditure and trend weight are estimates, not measurements.
For general tracking, not diagnosis or treatment (healthDisclaimer).

Photo logging estimates foods and portions; the user reviews the draft. It only works on phones with Apple Intelligence (photos need iOS 27 on eligible iPhones, descriptions iOS 26 or later) or Gemini Nano on supported Android phones. Phone timing has not been measured, so make no speed claims.
Label scanning targets US Nutrition Facts panels; other layouts are not checked systematically.
Packaged food data comes from Open Food Facts under ODbL 1.0 and USDA data is CC0. Attribution is required, and label accuracy of community data cannot be guaranteed.
Targets stay within 1,500 to 5,000 kcal a day; check-ins hold on sharp weight jumps or implausible expenditure.

privacyFacts: No account and no sign-in: there is no auth code or auth dependency in src, modules, targets or package.json.
No network calls in app code: a grep of src, modules, targets and plugins finds no fetch, XMLHttpRequest, WebSocket or remote URL (only podspec homepages and a plist DTD).
No analytics, crash reporting, ad or purchase SDKs in package.json dependencies.
Drink logs and preferences live on the device in a SQLite database (water-track.db) through expo-sqlite and Drizzle (src/db/provider.tsx, src/db/schema.ts).
The app has no application-level backup or export; uninstalling or clearing app storage removes local records (README Database changes; en.json localNote).

Health sync is off by default and turned on from Settings; permission prompts appear only when enabling it, and automatic sync never prompts (settings.tsx connect(); schema healthEnabled default false).
The app writes health data only to Apple Health or Health Connect on the device; disconnecting stops future exports and leaves already exported records in the health app (en.json disconnectNote).
Reminders are off by default and are local notifications; the app never requests a push token and uses no push server or account (src/lib/notifications.ts; schema remindersEnabled default false).
The Apple Intelligence schedule setup runs Apple's on-device model; the routine description never leaves the device (modules/schedule-intelligence).
The Apple Watch talks to the iPhone directly through WatchConnectivity (targets/watch/expo-target.config.js frameworks; WatchStore.swift sendMessage and transferUserInfo).

readoutSpecimen.meta: Non-alcoholic fluids count toward your goal

caveats: Hydration progress measures logged intake, not physiological hydration (en.json goalNote).
The default 2,500 mL goal is editable and is not a personalized recommendation.
Drinks containing alcohol do not count toward the fluid goal; coffee and tea do.
Caffeine and strength values on presets are estimates; the app tells users to check the label (en.json defaultsNote).

The BAC estimate is off by default, needs a body weight (entered manually or read from the health app), uses a simplified Widmark calculation, and is not a measurement. It must never be used to decide whether to drive or whether someone is sober, even at 0.000% (en.json bacWarning).
Health Connect exports fluids and caffeine only; alcohol and BAC are not exported on Android.

Background sync and background reminder rescheduling run when iOS or Android allows; execution can be delayed and is not guaranteed after force-quitting. Automatic retries after a failed sync happen only while the app is open.
Reminders are scheduled up to 60 ahead (about four days); if the app goes unopened for several days, reminders stop once those run out.

Plain-language routine setup, including the English phrase reader, is shown only where Apple Intelligence is available (iOS 26 or later, an eligible device, Apple Intelligence on). It is hidden on Android and older iPhones, where the schedule is set with time pickers.
The Apple Watch app needs the iPhone app; there is no watch-only install.
Presets include brand names (Monster, Red Bull, Celsius, Alani Nu); marketing should not imply endorsement.

Naming: the current build is named "VECTOR HYDRATION" with home-screen label "HYDRATE" (app.json, ios Info.plist). "Vector Hydration" / "Hydration" is the recommended family name in docs/design-system.md, applied only after owner sign-off.
README lists device acceptance checks (native permissions, background execution, remote edit and delete, watch and reminder flows) that must pass before release.
notYetShipped: A Wear OS app: README says there is no Wear OS app yet. The mirrored reminder "Log water" button on Android watches is still on the device acceptance list.
Alcohol and BAC export to Health Connect: the current React Native Health Connect bridge does not expose those record types.
Any payment, one-time purchase or licensing flow: none exists in code.
App Store or Google Play availability: the repo shows version 1.0.0 with device acceptance checks, Google Play health declarations and a published privacy policy still needed before distribution.
A web build: browser SQLite is not configured (README); app.json only sets a favicon.
An iPad layout: ios.supportsTablet is false.
Home-screen widgets or Live Activities for this app: no widget target exists (targets/ has only watch and _shared).
Backup, export or cloud sync of drink logs: data has no application-level backup.
The rename to "Vector Hydration" with home-screen label "Hydration": recommended in docs/design-system.md, pending owner sign-off; the build still says VECTOR HYDRATION / HYDRATE.
